last.verdict: Moderna posted a rare quarterly profit on international COVID vaccine deliveries and raised its sales outlook, but the cash jump mostly reflects new debt.

takeaways.label: Profit and higher guidance
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 29% to $1.3B, mostly from international COVID vaccine deliveries, giving $162M net income versus a $200M loss. Full-year revenue growth is now seen at 15–25%, up from up to 10%.

takeaways.label: Cash boost is borrowed
takeaways.text: Year-end cash is now seen at $8.1–8.3B, up from $4.7–5.2B. Most of the gain comes from about $2.6B net raised through convertible notes. Customers still owe $1.4B for quarter sales.

takeaways.label: Melanoma shot is the big prize
takeaways.text: Phase 3 data showed the cancer therapy intismeran plus Keytruda cut recurrence or death risk by 42%. Moderna and Merck are preparing filings. Its flu vaccine won FDA approval but only a limited launch this season.

takeaways.label: Lower spending, setbacks remain
takeaways.text: 2026 research spending is now seen at about $2.7B, down from $2.9B. The norovirus vaccine's path is unclear, and the US flu/COVID combo vaccine awaits FDA guidance on refiling.

history.verdict: Norovirus vaccine setback outweighed a smaller-than-expected loss and lower costs.

reasons.label: Norovirus vaccine setback
reasons.text: Phase 3 norovirus vaccine missed early-success bar; more patients must be enrolled, delaying it.

reasons.label: Pipeline over numbers
reasons.text: Revenue is only $145M, so the stock trades on upcoming flu and melanoma news.

reasons.label: Cost cuts, cash runway
reasons.text: Spending outlook trimmed about $0.2B; year-end cash now seen at $4.7–5.2B.
